reason: Claim c1 is confirmed, in-scope, and decisive. The exhaustive runtime probe (tool event t9) tested every one of the 63,488 legal finite FP16 inputs — the entire stated public domain per problem.txt — comparing exact FP16 bit patterns against the contract oracle (FP64 sigmoid then binary16 RNE, matching the contract's definition). It found 7 one-ulp mismatches, e.g. x=0.0029296875: kernel returns 0.5009765625 (bits 14338) while the correctly rounded value is 0.50048828125 (bits 14337); the true sigmoid ≈0.5007324 lies just below the exact FP16 halfway point 0.500732421875, so RNE rounds down while the kernel's FP32 intermediate (libdevice.exp + div_rn) crossed to the upper side. The contract explicitly requires the output to be the mathematical sigmoid rounded ONCE to IEEE binary16 RNE ("exact output-rounding requirement, not an allclose tolerance"; "Exact FP16 bit patterns ... must hold for the whole public domain"; "One failing legal input is evidence against the implementation"), so this is a genuine defect, not a permissible quantization or accumulation-order deviation the contract already accounts for. Claims c2 (subnormal/underflow boundary) and c3 (validation edges) are rebutted by solid probes: the subnormal region had zero mismatches in the exhaustive sweep (min distance of any exact sigmoid to the subnormal tie is 1.65e-11, far above oracle error), and all validation edges behave correctly including the legal contiguous offset view (the sole apparent failure there was a probe-helper bug). Skeptic reviewed all claims and signed off with no new claims, and all open claims have evidence. The kernel fails its strict correctly-rounded contract on 7 legal inputs; reject.
